blinding_guess.why: From this snapshot alone: the attitude quaternion is sent after UAS::transform_frame_enu_ned, which at this revision is FRAME_ROTATE_Q = quaternion_from_rpy(M_PI, 0.0, 0.0), a +PI rotation about X, applied as FRAME_ROTATE_Q * q * FRAME_ROTATE_Q.inverse() (uas_frame_conversions.cpp:24-25, 61-64). A +PI roll maps the ENU axes to East-South-Down, not North-East-Down, so an ENU attitude conjugated this way reaches the FCU with a yaw offset, and no separate body-axis (FLU to FRD) conversion is applied to the orientation. The comment at setpoint_attitude.cpp:119 ('Eigen use same convention as mavlink: w x y z') is also wrong about Eigen's x,y,z,w coefficient order, although lines 125-128 copy w,x,y,z explicitly and so work around it. The same +PI roll applied to twist.angular (:148) is a plausible body-axis flip, and the type_mask constants (:116, :145, :162) are consistent with their own comments, so q is the element I suspect. This is a code-reading inference only; nothing outside the workspace was consulted.
